To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PCA of the VAE representations of the training data consistently discovers interpretable latent directions in language VAEs.

(1) PCA of latent representations of training data discovers interpretable text controls; (2) this approach is simple, fast, and does not require training; and (3) it outperforms coordinate directions and random directions.

1) we can find meaningful latent directions in text VAEs by running PCA on VQA representations; 2) the discovered directions are interpretable; 3) the approach works for different text VAEs and datasets; 4) we show that our approach outperforms coordinate and random directions, and 5) the directions discovered by our approach are better than the ones discovered by existing methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how to find interpretable latent directions in language VAEs.
the following questions: 1. Can we discover interpretable directions in the latent space of language VAEs? 2. Can we find these directions without supervision?

the following questions: How can we discover interpretable directions in the latent space of text VAEs? Can we find directions in the latent spaces of text VAE models that are interpretable? What are these directions, and what do they represent?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the unsupervised discovery approach for finding meaningful directions in the latent space of language models, as proposed in this paper, is promising and has the potential to become a valuable tool for the community.
we have shown that the latent space of VAEs is not empty, and it can be filled with meaningful directions.
our approach allows to compare models and to discover meaningful latent controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to discover interpretable latent controls for language generation models without supervision.
we show that language VAEs can be used for unsupervised discovery interpretable latent controls.
we show how to find interpretable latent controls for language VAEs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
language models are not that far behind image models when it comes to latent spaces.
latent space interpretability is not an innate property of a language model but can be learned.
language latent spaces are not as interpretable as image latent spaces and there is room for improvement.
